LESSON: WRITING 7.4.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.4: Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of writing

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of writing. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should we punctuate our speech or writing correctly?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the comma and double quotation marks in a text
2. use the comma and the double quotation marks correctly in oral and written texts

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: WRITING 7.4.1 MECHANICS OF WRITING
This lesson teaches Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of writing for Grade 6 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

STUDY STEPS
1. identify the comma and double quotation marks in a text
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
2. use the comma and the double quotation marks correctly in oral and written texts
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of writing using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of writing above.
2. Explain Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of writing to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of writing.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of writing with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Writing 7.4.1 Mechanics of writing important for a Grade 6 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should we punctuate our speech or writing correctly?
2. Which punctuation marks do you use frequently?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify the comma and double quotation marks in a text
2. use the comma and the double quotation marks correctly in oral and written texts

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
